findings.failure_scenario: A consumer migrating off the deprecated public constant ULL reads the @deprecated note 'use _ULL' and writes JSONWire._ULL; this fails to compile with 'private access in JSONWire'. The published Javadoc also renders a link to a member absent from the public API docs (broken anchor), so no usable replacement for ULL is documented.
findings.summary: The new deprecation Javadoc on the public field ULL directs users to the private field _ULL, which is inaccessible outside the class.

findings.failure_scenario: Input JSON containing a number in exponent notation, e.g. {"x": 1e3}: copyNumber reads '1' and stops at 'e' (the switch's default case), then expectComma throws IORuntimeException "Expected a comma or '}' not a 'e'". A developer relying on the documented exponent support for scientific-notation values gets a parse failure the Javadoc says cannot happen.
findings.summary: New copyNumber Javadoc claims the method reads an optional exponent, but the parsing switch has no 'e'/'E' case, so exponent notation is not read.

findings.failure_scenario: escape0(s, Quotes.SINGLE), a call the superclass contract permits, emits an unescaped double-quote character inside a JSON double-quoted string, producing malformed JSON — exactly the behavior the new Javadoc rules out by stating the quotes parameter is ignored.
findings.summary: New escape0 Javadoc claims the quotes parameter is ignored, but the 'case "' branch checks ch == quotes.q, so the output depends on that parameter.

findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the Javadoc expects sb to hold both the key and the value following the colon; the actual method (JSONWire.java:1382-1392) reads only the key text into sb and never reads the value, so code written against the documented contract misinterprets sb's contents.
findings.summary: New readTypeDefinition Javadoc says the method reads the '@type' key and its string value into sb, but the method reads only the key into sb and consumes the colon.
